newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Victorias seen surviving after debt relief.
newsitem.headline: Victorias seen surviving after debt relief.

text.p: The Philippines' decision to grant Victorias Milling Corp (VMC) a reprieve from its debts gives it breathing space and will allow the company to survive in the already shaky local sugar industry, analysts said on Wednesday.
"The suspension of Victorias' debt payments would give it much relief," Sugar Regulatory Administration chief Wilson Gamboa told Reuters.

On Tuesday, the Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the petition of Victorias to suspend payments on its debts totalling 5.07 billion pesos ($192 million) after talks of a rehabilitation with its 32 bank creditors in recent weeks bogged down.
The SEC also approved on June 24 the proposed suspension on the payments of the 2.196 billion pesos worth of debt of Victorias' trading arm North Negros Marketing Corp.
"Victorias is not insolvent...it has only liquidity problems," Gamboa said.
Victorias said it has total assets of 7.1 billion pesos against total liabilities of 5.07 billion.

Victorias, the country's largest sugar miller and one of biggest in Asia, ran into financial troubles in 1995 due to the slump in the local sugar industry because of rising competition from cheaper imports, the SEC said.
But Gamboa said Victorias had an edge over the other 35 sugar mills in the country because it had the best infrastructure.
Analysts attributed the fall of Victorias to its diversification into non-sugar businesses, including cut flowers, which they said were mostly funded by bank borrowings.
Jasmine Juanico, analyst at Anscor Hagedorn Securities, said the SEC suspension on the debt payments of Victorias defused threats by some banks to foreclose its properties.
Bank creditors of Victorias and its trading arm said the intervention by the SEC would enable some creditors without collateral to get their money back.
Victorias and North Negros have both asked the SEC to form a committee to help them to get back on their feet.
"Banks are now looking forward to a viable rehabilitation plan for Victorias," an official at one of the creditor banks said.
JG Summit Holdings Inc, the investment arm of tycoon John Gokongwei, has expressed keen interest in taking over Victorias.
